question: What is the defining characteristic of a C union, unlike a struct?
options: A union can contain function pointers only
A union's members must all be the same type
A union cannot be used inside functions
All members of a union share the same memory location, so writing to one member overwrites the others
explanation: Unlike a struct (where each member has its own storage), a union allocates a single shared block of memory sized for its largest member — all members overlap the same bytes.
